CNN live blog — updated 15:58 BST 26 Sep 2026 (10:58 AM EDT, Sat September 26, 2026)

HEADLINE: Nor'easter thrashes Northeast coast with strong wind and coastal flooding

A strong, early season nor'easter has arrived in the Northeast and is delivering a prolonged stretch of strong wind, soaking rain and coastal flooding through the weekend. Tides are rising around Saturday's full moon, worsening coastal impacts.

KEY FACTS FROM LIVE POSTS (times relative to 15:58 BST update):
- "More than 85,000 customers without power as wind picks up across the Northeast" (post ~8 min before 15:58 BST)
- Atlantic City roadways seeing "extreme flooding," but water is receding. Strong and persistent winds up to 45 mph have pushed the water more than 3 feet above even the normal high tide (storm surge). Flooding was at the 8 a.m. high tide.
- Gusty winds, periods of heavy rain and moderate to major coastal flooding — enough to inundate roads and vulnerable homes — from Virginia to New England.
- The storm has brought coastal flooding from North Carolina to New Jersey since Wednesday, with conditions expected to worsen through the weekend as wind gusts reach up to 60 mph and some areas see up to 5 inches of rain.
- Floodwater inundated Point Pleasant, New Jersey, on Saturday morning; a partially-submerged car sat on a flooded street. Watson Creek in neighbouring Manasquan, New Jersey, hit major flood stage around Saturday morning's high tide. Flooding will recede in the afternoon and return during the next high tide, around 8 p.m. ET. Tidal flooding will continue in the area through at least Monday morning.
- Floodwaters surrounded homes in a Tuckerton, New Jersey, neighbourhood.
- New York Governor Kathy Hochul warned anyone who goes near water this weekend is "gambling with their life". QUOTE (Hochul): "Stay out of the water. Stay away from the water." Coastal flooding remains the biggest concern for the state, according to the governor, who said the worst flooding is expected during Saturday morning's high tide. Hochul also noted that while it has only rained around half an inch so far, "much more is coming." She warned it would be a "longer scale event" and told residents to prepare — "That means flashlights."
- Storm doors ready at Coney Island and Howard Beach MTA stations.
- Fire Island ferry company suspends service.
- Residents in low-lying New Jersey shore community (Sea Bright) urged to relocate to higher ground; community anticipating 40-50mph winds. Sea Bright Mayor Brian Kelly said Friday the Shrewsbury "will most certainly flood throughout the weekend".
- Showers will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain, with isolated higher amounts. The storm finally departs Tuesday afternoon. Worst impacts from now through Sunday morning.
- Music festivals in Maryland and New York cancelled; Ed Sheeran's concerts at Gillette Stadium cancelled.
- Light to moderate rain falling from Boston to New York City and Philadelphia Saturday morning.
- Nor'easters typically form between Georgia and New Jersey within 100 miles east or west of the East Coast (NOAA). Most common between September and April. While nor'easters are not unusual in September, a storm of this intensity is more typical in the winter than in early fall.
- SEPARATELY (CBS News video billing, same day): Hurricane Nolo bearing down on Hawaii's Big Island; "Hurricane Nolo could bring catastrophic, life-threatening floods" to Hawaii.
